name: Piscis Austrinus
introduction: is the Southern Fish, said to be the parent of the two fish of Pisces. It drinks the water poured by Aquarius. Its brightest star, Fomalhaut, shines alone in a dim autumn sky.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Fomalhaut](hip:113368), 25 light-years away, is surrounded by a ring of dust, much like a younger, larger Kuiper Belt. The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have imaged its dusty belts in detail.
Fomalhaut is part of a wide triple system: [TW Piscis Austrini](id:cns5-5660), an orange dwarf, and a red dwarf travel through space with it.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Epsilon Piscis Austrini](hip:111954) is a blue giant, and [Beta Piscis Austrini](hip:111188) a white star.
The red dwarf [Lacaille 9352](id:lacaille-9352), about 11 light-years away, is one of the nearest stars, with fast motion across the sky and at least two planets.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: In 2008, Hubble seemed to have photographed a planet, Fomalhaut b, inside the dust ring. Later observations showed it fading and spreading out: it was most likely an expanding cloud of debris from a collision between two icy bodies.
